claims.text: A sub-micron hBN-enriched nanocomposite coating can be deposited onto CoCrFeNi by physical vapor deposition or an equivalent method.
Applying an hBN-enriched coating to CoCrFeNi will generate an adaptive tribolayer.
The tribolayer will be hBN-rich and have a lamellar structure.
The hBN-rich tribolayer will persist or reform throughout sliding from 25 to 800 °C.
hBN acts as a solid-lubricant phase with low shear strength.
The layered structure of hBN facilitates easy interfacial shear at both low and high temperatures.
At elevated temperatures, surface oxidation can stabilize the tribolayer by forming a protective boundary.
A stabilized tribolayer will provide continuous lubrication and mitigate wear.
The hBN-coated alloy will have a consistently lower coefficient of friction than uncoated CoCrFeNi throughout 25–800 °C.
The hBN-coated alloy will have a lower wear rate than uncoated CoCrFeNi throughout 25–800 °C.
Uncoated CoCrFeNi experiences increased friction and wear at one or both ends of the stated temperature range.
Inadequate lubrication contributes to the baseline alloy's increased friction and wear.
Increasing oxidation at high temperature contributes to increased friction and wear of the uncoated alloy.
The proposed performance claim is bounded to dry sliding in ambient air under moderate load and controlled speed from 25 to 800 °C.
Successful operation requires the coating to remain adherent and chemically stable during the specified tribological tests.

contradictions.description: The mechanism describes elevated-temperature oxidation as stabilizing a protective tribolayer and mitigating wear, whereas the baseline attributes increased high-temperature friction and wear to increasing oxidation. Different behavior for coated and uncoated surfaces could reconcile these statements, but that distinction is not explicitly developed.
